C016.story: A 1985 Costa Rican 5-colón coin. The front shows the national coat of arms, with its ships, volcanoes and seven stars, and the words AMERICA CENTRAL inside a seven-sided frame; the back shows the value with coffee branches, B.C.C.R. (the central bank), and the value in Braille for blind users. Struck in stainless steel.

C343.continent_line: North America · Country: Costa Rica · ISO: CR
C343.label: Costa Rica · 2008 · 10 Colones
C343.notes: Both sides photographed in the holder. Obverse reads REPUBLICA DE COSTA RICA around the arms with 2008 below; reverse reads 10 COLONES over a coffee-branch wreath, Braille dots beneath, B.C.C.R. along the bottom rim. The pale aluminium color and the round (not heptagonal) rim separate it from the collection's 1985 5 colones. The aluminium BCCR type is the only Costa Rica 10 colones struck in 2008: the brass-plated and aluminium-nickel-bronze strikes of the same design family ended in 2002, and the stainless-steel successor is dated 2021. No mint mark appears on either side.
C343.story: A Costa Rican 10 colones from 2008, struck in feather-light aluminium. One side carries the national arms: seven stars for the seven provinces, three volcanoes, a sunrise, and the sea on either side for the two oceans Costa Rica sits between. The other side states the value twice over, once in big numerals and once in Braille dots under the word COLONES, so the coin can be read by touch. These aluminium pieces were everyday small change by the hundreds of millions; Costa Rica later switched the denomination to stainless steel to cut costs.
